thread:
katie-support: FYI customer (acct: redwood-acme) opened a billing escalation — they say the Usage -> Tokens chart is showing higher totals than the raw API metrics. They selected region=eu-west-1 but totals look global. ticket: https://redwood.support/t/2345
mike-frontend: can you paste the tenant id and exact filters they used? also screenshot if available
katie-support: tenant_id: tenant_58b7
filters: region=eu-west-1, model=redwood-small-v2, version=2025-11-02
screenshot attached in ticket
james-backend: quick sanity check from metrics API (should be authoritative):
```
curl -s "https://api.redwood.com/metrics?tenant=tenant_58b7&region=eu-west-1&model=redwood-small-v2&from=2026-03-10&to=2026-03-11"
```
Returns counts scoped to eu-west-1. So likely a dashboard/frontend or aggregator cache mismatch, not the core metrics store.
olivia-sre: is this tenant the only reporter? any dashboard renderer errors around spike time?
katie-support: only this tenant reported so far. They said the console charts were slow and then showed inflated totals after a traffic spike.
lee-analytics: heads-up — we rolled out a small change yesterday that normalizes region keys in the analytics ingest layer (maps short keys like `eu` -> `eu-west-1`). If the dashboard client is still sometimes sending `eu` shorthand then aggregator cache keys will differ.
mike-frontend: pls paste the network payload when they clicked EU. I want to confirm whether UI sent full key or shorthand.
katie-support: customer devtools: `GET /dashboard/usage?tenant=tenant_58b7&region=eu&model=redwood-small-v2&from=...` — UI sent `region=eu` (shorthand) not the canonical name.
james-backend: that explains it. Aggregator caches use normalized `eu-west-1` keys (rollout-2026-03-16). When ui uses `eu`, cache lookup misses and code falls back to global precomputed buckets after a short timeout, resulting in inflated totals.
lee-analytics: reproducer I ran locally:
1) enable feature flag `region-normalization=v2` on analytics-service
2) dashboard requests with `region=eu`
3) aggregator normalizes internally but cache lookup ordering caused a miss then fallback to `*` global bucket after ~30s
Logs:
```
[2026-03-16T21:42:01Z] cache_lookup key=tenant_58b7|eu-west-1|redwood-small-v2 miss
[2026-03-16T21:42:01Z] fallback_to_global=TRUE
```
olivia-sre: fallback path should be conservative. Looks like a race: normalization happening in one place but cache key computed earlier in the flow in another shard. Could be rollout ordering inconsistency.
mike-frontend: mitigation options: 1) quick client patch to always send normalized region name, 2) rollback the analytics normalization flag, 3) patch aggregator lookup to normalize earlier. Which is least risky short-term?
lee-analytics: immediate step: roll back the normalization flag (low blast radius) and push a tiny frontend patch to normalize on the client. Rollback stops future misses but won't repair already-cached global aggregates.
james-backend: long term: ensure canonicalization at ingress for both UI and telemetry, and add a backfill re-aggregation job for affected tenant/region windows. I'll prepare a one-off backfill plan.
katie-support: customer reports ~12% higher token usage in the console for that day and asking for billing adjustment if backfill reduces counts. They want ETA.
olivia-sre: action items (owners):
- [P1] rollback analytics region-normalization flag (lee-analytics)
- [P2] frontend client quick patch to normalize region param (mike-frontend)
- [P2] one-off backfill/re-aggregation for tenant_58b7 and other hit tenants (james-backend)
- support: keep customer updated and collect any other impacted tenants (katie-support)
mike-frontend: opened tiny PR to normalize region on client and guard against shorthand: https://github.com/redwood-inference/frontend/pull/3921
lee-analytics: rollback in progress
deploy-bot: rollback triggered by lee-analytics on analytics-service @ 2026-03-17T02:14:22Z
lee-analytics: rollback completed, analytics-service back to previous behavior. Posting follow-up logs to #eng-ml.
james-backend: started backfill for tenant_58b7 for window 2026-03-10..2026-03-11, initial estimate ~12m, will update when done.
katie-support: told customer we patched rollback and will follow up within 24h with backfill/billing outcome. Keeping ticket open.
support-bot: Escalation created: ESC-8742 | severity P1. linked ticket: https://redwood.support/t/2345
mike-frontend: note for postmortem: root cause = asymmetric normalization during staggered rollout + cache fallback path too eager. Suggested fixes: canonicalize filters at ingress, make cache fallback conservative, and sequence rollouts to avoid asymmetric states.
lee-analytics: will collect logs and write a short postmortem in #postmortems after backfill confirms counts.
katie-support: tagging @account-team for potential billing outreach if backfill reduces billed tokens.
